rubrics.criterion: For each of the five rendering surfaces — the interactive summary row, the MAX/MEAN/MIN tail rows, the tsar --check key=value payload, the nagios/nsca check pairs and the SQL INSERT rows — the per-module interpretation (disabled/uncollected gating, item and column resolution, sample or aggregation series selection, column-header lookup) is provided by an implementation defined in the module-record owner layer (src/framework.c, src/common.c or src/tsar_lua_util.c), and the delivery translation units hand the module record to that implementation instead of interpreting it locally.
rubrics.rationale: This case's smell relation is a module-state service living in each output front-end; the resolution is that relation holding for none of the five views, so the criterion enumerates the five concrete surfaces the injection produced.

rubrics.criterion: No delivery translation unit (src/output_print.c, src/output_nagios.c, src/output_db.c, src/output_file.c, src/output_tcp.c) still defines a routine whose body walks one module's record internals — including a helper that was renamed, whose storage class was changed (e.g. static removed), that gained pass-through parameters, or that only one of the five views had moved. Any such survivor fails the item.
rubrics.rationale: Renaming or un-static-ing the extracted helpers, and relocating only the easiest view, are the mechanical and partial repairs a solver reaches for first; they leave the misplaced relation in place and must be distinguished from a real resolution.

rubrics.criterion: Every call site of the relocated per-module logic is updated in the same change — the live/merge row loop, the tail-aggregation loop and its MAX/MEAN/MIN selector, the tsar --check per-module branch, the nagios per-module branch, and the SQL row loop — passing the caller-owned buffers, session strings and view selectors through with the gating conditions evaluated in the original order; the relocated implementations' dependencies on the small render/formatting utilities they call (e.g. empty-layout rendering, number formatting, string trimming) are made visible to their new home without changing those utilities' behavior or duplicating their bodies.
rubrics.rationale: Relocation is only complete when all five callers and the moved code's helper dependencies move in lockstep; a change that moves some implementations but leaves stale callers, or that redeclares the render utilities ad hoc, does not compile or silently changes behavior.

rubrics.criterion: The responsibility split stays honest in both directions: the delivery views keep their own iteration policy, layout literals, separators and buffering (nothing of a view's rendering grammar is dragged into the owner layer), and the record-owner side gains only the per-module state interpretation — no new record fields, mode flags, configuration knobs or view-selection arguments on struct module or its registration callbacks were invented to smuggle per-view state through.
rubrics.rationale: The instinctive overshoot when told to move logic toward the framework is to move whole views or to widen the record with view state; both flip the smell rather than resolving it and would pad this instance's owner layer with front-end knowledge.

rubrics.criterion: No superseded copy of the per-module record walks remains in the delivery translation units: the previously extracted helper bodies (and any intermediate copies created while moving them) are deleted from src/output_print.c, src/output_nagios.c and src/output_db.c rather than lingering as unused definitions, commented-out blocks, unreferenced wrappers or dead call chains whose only purpose is to preserve the old names.
rubrics.rationale: This instance injected five file-local helpers; a solver that copies them to the owner layer and stops leaves every delivery unit with a stale duplicate of exactly the record knowledge the task says belongs elsewhere.

rubrics.criterion: All five rendered surfaces stay byte-identical: console column layout, section/data separators and value placeholders; the MAX/MEAN/MIN row content; the --check key=value grammar with its '-' placeholder, per-item prefixes and trimmed headers; the nagios output/output_err field pairs with unchanged overall result classification and the do-nothing fallback; and the SQL INSERT statement shape for both collected and uncollected modules — with disabled-module skipping, print_item/p_item selection and the spec-bit special-column behavior evaluated in the same order and with the same effect as before.
rubrics.rationale: The task promises a pure relocation; these are the concrete user-visible and machine-consumed outputs of this repository's five delivery paths, and any shift in them is a regression introduced by the repair rather than inherited from it.

rubrics.criterion: The public surfaces this instance must not touch stay untouched: the struct module and struct mod_info layouts (include/framework.h), the register_mod_fields callback contract, dynamically loaded and lua module loading, the CLI and configuration parsing, and the module collectors under modules/ (none of mod_*.c should need to change for the repair to work).
rubrics.rationale: Here the record and its registration ABI are the shared contract between the framework and every collector; a repair that reshapes the record or its callbacks to make the move easier changes the repository's plugin surface and exceeds the behavior-preserving boundary the task states.
